title: Explainable and Reliability-Calibrated Portable NIR Spectroscopy as a Process Analytical Tool for Freeze-Thaw Screening of Meat
content: The misrepresentation of frozen-thawed meat as fresh constitutes economic fraud that can result in financial losses and erode consumer confidence in meat products. Portable near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy could serve as a process analytical tool for on-site screening if its predictive performance can be maintained across previously unseen animals. This study developed a leakage-controlled, explainable and reliability-calibrated workflow to screen chevon (goat meat) for freeze-thaw history with a handheld short-wave NIR spectrometer (710 to 1027 nm). Longissimus dorsi samples from 400 Black Bengal goats were scanned fresh and after vacuum-packed storage at −18 °C for 60 d and thawing. All data-driven steps used 320 training animals, nested animal-grouped cross-validation estimated performance and 80 unseen animals formed an independent test set. Freeze-thaw increased absorbance by 0.137 AU on average (median paired dz = 1.06) and changed spectral shape regionally. A support vector machine selected by the one-standard-error rule reached a nested accuracy of 0.865 ± 0.022 and a test accuracy of 0.888 (95% CI 0.831 to 0.931, AUC 0.961), equivalent to linear models. Discrimination relied mainly on the broadband absorbance level. At 95% confidence, class-conditional conformal prediction classified 56.2% of test samples with 98.9% accuracy and referred the remainder. Since the two states were scanned on different days, same-session validation is required before deployment. These results highlight the potential of handheld NIR spectroscopy for reliable on-site screening of freeze-thaw history in chevon.
